{
  "approach": "query",
  "change": "Refactor the list_notes function in app/db.py to use SQL-based filtering and pagination instead of in-memory Python processing. Replace the current pattern of fetching all rows and filtering in Python with a single SQL query that applies WHERE clauses for search_text (using LIKE) and tags_filter (using JSON functions or string matching), and uses LIMIT/OFFSET for pagination. This eliminates the O(N) scan and JSON parsing for all rows when only a small subset is needed.",
  "hypothesis": "The current implementation fetches all notes from the database and filters them in Python, which causes O(N) database reads and JSON parsing for every request, regardless of the limit. By moving the filtering and pagination logic into the SQL query, we reduce the amount of data transferred from the database and avoid parsing JSON for rows that will be discarded. This should significantly reduce cumulative time for list_notes, especially as the number of notes grows.",
  "risks": [
    "SQL LIKE queries are case-sensitive by default, which matches the current behavior, but must be implemented carefully to avoid SQL injection (use parameterized queries).",
    "Filtering tags in SQL requires parsing the JSON array stored in the tags column. This may be slower than simple string matching if not optimized, but should still be faster than parsing all JSON in Python.",
    "The current implementation uses 'all' tags must match. The SQL query must correctly implement this logic, possibly using multiple EXISTS or IN clauses.",
    "If the database is small, the overhead of complex SQL might not yield significant improvements, but it will not degrade performance compared to the current O(N) approach."
  ],
  "schema_version": 1
}
